newsitem.title: UK: Moody's raises DG Bank short-term desposit rating.
newsitem.headline: Moody's raises DG Bank short-term desposit rating.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Friday it had raised the short-term bank desposit rating of Germany's Deutsche Genossenschaftsbank to Prime-1 from Prime 2.
Moody's also said it was confirming the bank's long-term deposit rating at A2 and its financial strength rating at D+.

Moody's said in a statement the upgrade of the short-term deposit rating reflected the improvement reached in DG Bank's financial performance after the extensive restructuring carried out within the bank since 1991.

The rating agency said DG Bank's restructuring followed "financial and franchise erosion" caused by business decisions which led to problems in asset quality, asset liability management and equity participation problems.

"Both asset quality and recurring profitability indicators have improved in recent years, although they still remain more modest than those of other regional banks of the German cooperative banking sector," Moody's said.
Liquidity remained acceptable but capitalisation remained weak, Moody's said.
The DG Bank group is Germany's seventh largest banking group with total consolidated assets of 290 billion, Moody's said.
